metadata.title: التقرير الوطني األردني عن الدراسة الدولية للرياضيات والعلوم لعام 2011 (TIMSS 2011)
metadata.venue: المركز الوطني لتنمية الموارد البشرية (NCHRD) - سلسلة منشورات المركز

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report describes TIMSS 2011 Jordan data collection using a two-stage probability proportional-to-size (PPS) sampling design with the school as the sampling unit and one or two Grade 8 classes selected randomly within each sampled school. The authors explicitly state that sampling weights were computed and taken into account in the analysis of results. However, the report does not provide the exact weight variable name(s) (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) nor any replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because this is a national report summarizing TIMSS results with descriptive comparisons and regression/correlation analyses, the manuscript does not detail whether weights were incorporated into any model-based estimation beyond the stated use of sampling weights.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This national report does not present any machine-learning modeling on PV-based achievement outcomes, and it does not describe plausible value generation/combination procedures (e.g., Rubin’s rules, PV1-only, PV averaging). Instead, it reports TIMSS achievement summaries (means, ranks, and proficiency-level percentages) and discusses relationships between derived questionnaire indicators and achievement using conventional statistical summaries. As a result, PV handling is not applicable to the extracted analytical content, and the report also does not document any missing-data strategy for the questionnaire or achievement variables.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is the set of Grade 8 students in Jordan who participated in TIMSS 2011, selected from MoE schools, private schools, and UNRWA schools. Sampling followed a two-stage PPS design: schools were sampled first, then one or two Grade 8 classes were selected randomly within each sampled school. The report does not specify additional exclusions (e.g., missing questionnaire items, incomplete test booklets) or any further analytic subsample restrictions beyond the Grade 8 and school-type inclusion.

data.outcome_summary: This Jordan national report for TIMSS 2011 (Grade 8) reports achievement summaries and subgroup comparisons rather than training machine-learning models. For science, Jordan’s mean is 449 versus an international mean of 477 (rank 28/45), and the report states a substantial decline from 2007 to 2011 of 33 points. For mathematics, Jordan’s mean is 406 versus an international mean of 467 (rank 35/45), with a reported decline of 21 points from 2007 to 2011. The report also uses conventional regression/correlation analyses to relate achievement to derived questionnaire indicators; for mathematics, R² is 0.083 (2007) and 0.135 (2011), and for science R² is 0.081 (2007) and 0.129 (2011). No ML algorithms, PV-combination procedures, or missing-data handling strategies are documented in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
